narrative:
The model estimates a 60% chance that you will leave your job, which is why your promotion request has been denied. This prediction is driven primarily by three key aspects of your profile that stood out compared to employees the system expected to stay.

Your total years of experience had the strongest influence, pushing the prediction toward leaving. With 6-10 years overall, you sit in a range where many people begin exploring new opportunities, unlike the majority of those predicted to stay who have only 1-5 years. This signals to the model that you may be at a natural career transition point.

Next, the time you have spent in your current role worked in the opposite direction, modestly pulling the prediction toward staying. Having 6-10 years in this organization is longer than most employees the model expects to remain, suggesting some established loyalty.

Finally, the fact that you have not received other job offers recently also nudged the outcome toward staying, though not enough to overcome the other signals. Most employees predicted to stay similarly report no external opportunities.

Taken together, the model sees your experience level as the main reason you might depart, despite your tenure here and lack of outside offers. The organization should discuss your career goals openly with you and explore whether additional responsibilities, better recognition, or clearer advancement paths could increase your sense of stability and satisfaction. You may also want to reflect on what would make staying feel like the right long-term choice.
